name: Puffing Billy Railway

facts.claim: Heritage steam railway on a 762 mm (2 ft 6 in) narrow-gauge line running 25.1 km from Belgrave to Gembrook through the Dandenong Ranges
Originally opened by Victorian Railways in 1900 and now run as a tourist railway
Lakeside station has a visitor centre with a cafe, gift shop and a gallery of steam artefacts

name: Dandenong Ranges National Park

facts.claim: Forested volcanic hills covered in Mountain Ash, the world's tallest flowering tree, a short drive or train ride from Melbourne
Home to wallabies, lyrebirds, wombats and the Powerful Owl
Includes the 1000 Steps (Kokoda Track Memorial Walk) from Ferntree Gully Picnic Area, plus Olinda Falls and Sherbrooke Falls
The whole park closes on days of Extreme or higher Fire Danger Rating

name: Sherbrooke Forest

facts.claim: Cool temperate rainforest section of Dandenong Ranges National Park with a creek-fed gully at Sherbrooke Falls
Sherbrooke Falls walk and Sherbrooke picnic ground are the main visitor points; falls are best after rain
Park closes on Extreme or higher fire danger days

name: William Ricketts Sanctuary

facts.claim: Forest sanctuary on Mount Dandenong with 92 ceramic sculptures by William Ricketts set among fern gullies and rock faces
Reopened its first stage on 3 August 2026 after being closed since a June 2021 storm; some areas remain closed for restoration
An audio tour can be hired at the sanctuary for $5
Managed by Parks Victoria as a heritage site

name: National Rhododendron Gardens

facts.claim: Now called Dandenong Ranges Botanic Garden (formerly the National Rhododendron Garden), a 50 hectare cool-climate garden at Olinda with views over the Yarra Valley
Holds over 15,000 rhododendrons, 12,000 azaleas, 3,000 camellias and 250,000 daffodils, in flower in spring and autumn
A 3.5 km paved circuit passes a pond and ornamental lake; the site also has a re-created Chelsea Flower Show Australian Garden and a 101 hectare arboretum

name: Olinda

facts.claim: Hilltop village and suburb in the Dandenong Ranges, about 41 km east of Melbourne CBD at 569 m elevation
Gateway to Olinda Falls and the national park forest walks, and next to the Dandenong Ranges Botanic Garden
